image_description: A close-up, side-profile view of a Nile crocodile resting on a sandy, debris-strewn bank. The crocodile's head is prominent on the left, showing a closed mouth with visible teeth interlocking along the jawline. The body extends to the right, covered in rough, armored scales (scutes) that catch the sunlight, creating high contrast between the illuminated dorsal side and the shadowed ventral side. Dry grass and twigs obscure parts of the lower body and foreground.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The snout tapers distinctly towards the nostrils, forming a V-shape characteristic of crocodiles rather than the U-shape of alligators. The head structure appears broad and robust.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed, and a clear row of interlocking teeth is visible along the jawline. The fourth tooth on the lower jaw appears to fit into a notch on the upper jaw, consistent with crocodilian anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While the eye is visible, the resolution and lighting conditions make it impossible to definitively confirm the presence of vertical slit pupils or the specific state of the nictitating membrane. It is partially obscured by shadow and angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The nostrils are clearly visible at the very end of the snout, raised slightly above the surface line.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the body shows a long, continuous form covered in thick, bony plates.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal scales are large, raised, and arranged in distinct rows, matching the description of osteoderms.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coloration is a mix of earthy browns and greys, and the texture is visibly rough and knobby.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The ventral side (belly) is largely obscured by shadows, dry grass, and the angle of the crocodile's position against the ground. Cannot be verified.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The limbs are mostly hidden beneath the body and obscured by foreground vegetation. No clear view of digits or webbing is available.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only the base of the tail is visible; the majority of the tail extends out of the frame to the right.

artifact_observations.reasoning: Some of the thin twigs in the immediate foreground appear slightly fused or lack distinct separation from the background sand in certain spots, suggesting minor generative blur or edge bleeding, though it could also be depth-of-field effects.

The highlight on the eye is somewhat diffuse and lacks the sharp specular reflection typical of a wet, mucous-covered eye in direct sunlight. The lighting on the snout tip is slightly flat compared to the high-contrast scutes behind it.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the species identification based on snout shape and scute pattern, distinguishing it from other crocodilians or alligators.
To assess the realism of the skin texture and lighting, specifically checking for AI-generated 'waxy' skin or inconsistent shadows.
To verify the structural integrity of the jawline and teeth interlocking, ensuring no fusion artifacts between teeth and gums.
To check if the foreground twigs are correctly positioned in front of the crocodile and not merging into its skin.

focus_areas: Edge separation between foreground debris and subject
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the eye detail; AI often struggles with realistic eye reflections in reptiles. Also, verify if the 'interlocking teeth' are structurally plausible or if they look like a single fused ridge. Check if the foreground grass has natural depth or if it looks painted on.

metadata.class_label: African crocodile, Nile crocodile, Crocodylus niloticus
